blocks.text: The chapter opens at Sinai, while Egypt is remembered as the land Israel has left. This beginning introduces a book whose principal movement runs from Sinai toward the plains of Moab.

Numbers is geographically organized around Israel's movement from preparation at Sinai, through Kadesh and the Transjordan, to preparation on the plains of Moab. The census in this chapter also has a literary counterpart in Numbers 26: together, the two censuses frame the transition from the generation counted at Sinai to the generation prepared for inheritance near Moab.

sections.title: A Census at the Beginning of the Journey

blocks.text: The census total and the implied scale of Israel's wilderness population have received substantially different literary and historical interpretations. Because the question remains disputed, the chapter's figures should be acknowledged as an interpretive difficulty without presenting any single reconstruction as settled.
